planner_plan.bridge_text: 寒风吹过莉娜的红大衣，让她想起了奶奶没讲完的故事。既然这棵树里藏着秘密的嗡嗡声，莉娜决定不再等待，毅然迈进了那树洞之中。

replacement_segments.text: 莉娜深吸一口气，拨开垂下的树皮帘子。在那棵像教堂一样高大的树洞里，竟然有一圈螺旋向下的木质台阶。台阶顶端坐着一只老灰狐狸，它穿着一件缝补过多次的绿色背心，正用那双深邃的眼睛盯着闯入者。那狐狸自称莫斯克，声音听起来就像秋天里干枯的落叶在摩擦，他警告莉娜说这棵树不是小女孩该来的地方，催促她赶紧回家，把那阵嗡嗡声彻底忘掉。可莉娜却倔强地摇摇头，说她还没听见那声音的真面目，怎么能轻易放弃呢？

replacement_segments.text: Mosk pointed a steady claw toward the door, but Lina reached into her pocket and pulled out the last apple of the season. Finally, he stood up, straightened his patched green vest, and stepped onto the first stair, silently inviting her to follow him down into the depths.

Deep in the hollow, the humming resolved into a soft, sorrowful song. A firefly the size of a robin lay upon a bed of velvet moss, her golden glow flickering like a dying candle. Mosk’s whiskers trembled as he looked at her. He whispered that she had been his friend once, but long ago, he had failed to bring her the medicine she needed. Ever since that winter, he had guarded this tree, too ashamed to face the light he had let fade.

results.label: real-world-concept-question
results.qa_answer: Moss is a soft, velvet-green carpet that grows in damp and quiet places. It feels just like a cushion for a tired firefly to rest her wings upon.

planner_plan.bridge_text: Just like that soft, velvet moss cushioning the firefly, the quiet of the tree seemed to wrap around them both. With the tiny creature resting safely, the air began to shimmer again.

replacement_segments.text: At the bottom of the stairs, the humming was a quiet song, and a firefly the size of a robin lay on a bed of soft, velvet-green moss. Her glow was fading, flickering like a dying candle. Mosk's whiskers trembled as he watched her. He whispered that she had been his friend once, but one winter long ago, he had failed to bring her medicine in time. He had been guarding the hollow tree ever since, too ashamed to face her until now.

Lina knelt beside the mossy bed and asked the firefly queen what she needed. A drop of warm milk and a kind word, the queen sighed; that was all medicine ever really was. Mosk hurried to fetch the milk in a tiny silver thimble, laying his paw gently beside hers. As she drank, the queen’s glow steadied and turned bright gold. The humming inside the tree shifted into a beautiful, unfamiliar tune, and for the first time in many years, Mosk hummed along.
